audience: evaluator_only; expose tasks/<id>.md and only the before source to the model

isolation.network: none; RQ Python joins only its dedicated Redis container's network-none namespace
isolation.mounts: selected source, dependencies, one check, and runner, all read-only
isolation.memory_per_container: 512 MiB, no swap allowance beyond memory
isolation.limitations: rootful Docker daemon with unprivileged containers; shared kernel, not a VM

environment.urllib3_build: Identical offline hatchling wheel build in /tmp from each source tree; SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=0.0.0+reproduction generates _version.py. Runtime imports the corresponding built source, not a published urllib3 wheel.

common_limitations: Published PRs and solution patches can contaminate training or retrieval data; novelty and non-memorization are not established.
This proves historical before/after behavior, not failure of an agent using an original Skill.
No model, GEPA, statistical model comparison, or hidden holdout evaluation was performed.
Only the recorded Python/platform/dependency combination and focused checks were run; no full compatibility matrix.
Model/evaluator separation is a packaging boundary, not enforcement if an agent can read the whole worktree. Never mount this entire directory or its .cache into a model execution sandbox.

candidates.commit_selection: actual first parent of merged squash commit; verified by Git object graph and identical behavioral regression
candidates.check_origin: upstream regression method unchanged; adapted wrapper plus two unchanged upstream pipeline controls
candidates.symptom: A generator containing a dependent and an independent job returns only the independent job.
candidates.expected_behavior: Return independent then dependent; preserve queue order; persist the dependent as DEFERRED in the deferred registry; retain internal/caller pipeline behavior.
candidates.recommendation_reason: Small production diff, actual Redis persistence and upstream regression, clear one-shot iterable contract.
candidates.project_d_handoff: Use a one-shot generator mixing dependent and independent jobs; check no loss/duplication, returned and queued order, deferred persistence, caller-owned commit boundaries. This pattern is not proof about any project_d implementation.
limitations: Does not exhaustively cover every iterable, dependency graph, or pipeline combination.
Initial attempt accidentally collected the whole imported TestQueue class, producing different test counts; it is excluded from final paired evidence.
The PR body discloses AI assistance; public patch existence must not be treated as novel unseen-agent evidence.

candidates.commit_selection: actual first parent of merged squash commit; verified by Git object graph and identical behavioral regression
candidates.check_origin: new evaluator-authored fault-injection integration check, not an upstream test
candidates.symptom: Dependent-enqueue failure leaves a real rate-limit slot allocated in both terminal failure paths. A swallowed first persistence error can permit follow-ups without the failed state being committed.
candidates.expected_behavior: Persist terminal failure before follow-ups; persistence failure prevents webhook/dependent/release actions; dependent-enqueue failure cannot prevent slot release; release errors are logged without undoing persistence.
candidates.recommendation_reason: Rich compact state/exception contract, but original integration setup includes Redis, worker executions, registries, and rate-limiter state. Use the verified original as an anchor for a separately tested mock.
candidates.project_d_handoff: Cross terminal failure/retry exhaustion with no fault, persist fault, first persist fault only, dependent registration fault, and slot release fault. Inspect durable state plus event trace; do not hardcode upstream helper names or mandate release-before-dependents.
limitations: Faults are deterministically injected before transaction execution; Pipeline.reset mirrors redis-py cleanup. Ambiguous connection loss after server commit is not modeled.
Webhook delivery and dependent execution are mocked; actual network delivery and a real worker process crash are not tested.
Tests verify a real slot is freed but not promotion of a waiting rate-limited job.
Stopped jobs, nonterminal retries, and maintenance-based recovery are outside this focused matrix.
Despite the PR title, the final patch does not move slot release ahead of dependent enqueueing; it isolates their exception handlers.
